headline: Munich robotics company RobCo passes a $1 billion valuation
summary: RobCo said on 5 October 2026 that it had passed a $1 billion valuation and that CEO Roman Hölzl had relocated to the United States. Reuters reported the valuation was based on a secondary sale of shares by employees to existing and new investors (including Cherry Ventures and the European Tech Collective) following a $100 million raise in January 2026; other outlets describe a mix of fresh capital and a secondary component. Up from about $500 million in January 2026.

sources.headline: German robot startup RobCo hits $1 billion valuation, CEO moves to US
RobCo hits $1B valuation as Sequoia, Lightspeed back Munich robotics maker

card.what_happened: RobCo, a Munich industrial-robotics company, said it has passed a $1 billion valuation (5 Oct 2026). The price was set mainly by employees selling existing shares to new and existing investors, after a $100M round in January 2026 at about $500M; reports differ on how much fresh money was involved.
card.why_it_matters: It shows strong investor appetite for 'physical AI' — robots that small and mid-sized factories can actually deploy — and sets a valuation benchmark for European robotics. It is a late-stage event: the early-stage opportunity was years ago.
card.the_company: RobCo builds modular industrial robots — a hardware kit plus software — that small and mid-sized manufacturers can configure for repetitive tasks.
card.vc_lesson: A 'unicorn' headline can come from a secondary share sale: it tells you what buyers paid per share, not how much the company raised.
watch_next: US expansion: the CEO moved to the US; production in Austin, a lab in San Francisco
The next product ('Alfie'), planned for March 2027

backcast.text: Years of research at TU Munich's robotics and AI chair underpin the later company (per the founders).
RobCo founded in Munich (2020) by Roman Hölzl, Paul Maroldt and Constantin Dresel, research assistants at TU Munich's robotics & AI chair — a TUM spinout.
Seed round (amount not public in free sources).
Series A, roughly $14–16M (sources differ; Sequoia led per the founders).
Series C, $100M, at about a $500M valuation (aggregator data).

learning: RobCo's earliest public signal was a TU Munich robotics spinout (2020), followed by a seed round (2021) — about five years before the unicorn headline and six years before Project Zero started (Sep 2026). By then RobCo was post-Series C: a benchmark, not an operational miss. Today a similar company would most likely surface through the university spinout sensors (TUM Venture Labs, UnternehmerTUM) or an incorporation on a watched name; by its first funding news (Series A, 2022) the earliest edge was already gone.
